modelResponse.episodeSummary: 79F, Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (RVR), warning severity, borderline hypotensive/hemodynamically unstable on norepinephrine
modelResponse.rhythm: Atrial Fibrillation with Rapid Ventricular Response (RVR)
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Narrow QRS, absent P waves, fibrillatory baseline
preEventNote: Sinus tachycardia earlier in shift; converted to AFib RVR as fever spiked
modelResponse.mechanism: Systemic inflammatory response and fever-induced sympathetic surge driving supraventricular tachycardia in a patient with underlying physiological stress.
contributingFactors: Sepsis (WBC 18.4 HIGH, Procalcitonin 6.2 HIGH, Lactate 3.1 HIGH)

rejectedAlternatives.why: TSH 1.8 mIU/L is within normal reference range (0.4–4.0)
K 3.6 mmol/L and Mg 1.8 mg/dL are within normal limits
Troponin T 0.03 is only mildly elevated; clinical picture is more consistent with systemic sepsis/fever

recommendedActions: Aggressive fluid resuscitation with IV crystalloids to address sepsis and hypotension
Optimize sepsis management (continue Piperacillin-tazobactam, monitor blood cultures)
Antipyretic administration (e.g., Acetaminophen) to reduce fever-driven sympathetic drive
Monitor electrolyte-driven rhythm stability (K and Mg)
Titrate vasopressors (Norepinephrine) based on MAP targets
Evaluate for rate control (e.g., Beta-blockers or Calcium Channel Blockers) only once patient is hemodynamically stabilized and volume-resuscitated
uncertainty: The exact trigger for the conversion from sinus tachycardia to AFib is likely the fever/sepsis, but the underlying susceptibility to arrhythmia is not fully characterized without prior ECGs.
